J U D G M E N T

This claim petition is filed by the petitioners claiming compensation of .80,00,000/- with interest from the date of petition till its realization for the death of Sri.Pavan Kumar.S S/o.Shankar.B, in road traffic accident.

2. The petition averments in brief is that on 02.02.2023 at about 5.00 p.m., when deceased was proceeding on a Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-53- EU-7001 as a pillion rider, driven by his friend Sri.Dommera Suresh on Anjanapura Double road, on Anjanapura- Kanakapura Road, near Narayanagarada Swamy Vivekananda Road Junction, a Concrete Mix Lorry bearing Regn.No.KA-05-AK-7058, driven by its driver at high speed in a rash and negligent manner, dashed against the motor cycle to its rear side resulting in accident.
Due to said accident, the petitioner and the rider were knocked down and the back wheel of lorry ran over the deceased due to which he sustained grievous injuries.

Thereafter, the deceased was shifted to Mathrushree Hospital and then shifted to Manipal Hospital, Jayanagar, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient and later succumbed to the injuries on 11.02.2023.

The petitioners have spent a sum of .22,50,000/-
towards treatment, medicine, Conveyance, transportation and funeral and obsequies ceremonies.
Prior to the accident, the deceased was hale and healthy and was a Civil Engineering Graduate and a merit student and working as Civil Engineering Contractor and earning a sum of .80,000/- per month.
Due to the death of deceased, the petitioners lost the bread earning member of the family and put to lot of mental agony.
The accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of lorry by its driver.
The respondent No.1 & 2, being the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to petitioners.
3. In spite of service of notice, respondent No.1 did not appear before the tribunal and hence, he has been placed ex-parte.
The respondent No.2 appeared before the tribunal through the counsel and filed the written statement.
4. In the Written Statement, the respondent No.2 denied the contents of claim petition specifically and categorically.
The respondent No.2 also denied age, occupation and income of deceased as well as place, time and manner of accident.
Further the respondent No.2 contended that the petition filed by the petitioners is not maintainable either in law or on facts and same is liable to be dismissed.

Further contended that the accident occurred solely due to rider of motor cycle, who was riding the same in a rash and negligent manner without putting indicator/signal and suddenly took Shankar.B vs Raghavendra Ready Mix Concrete on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145092162/
2 U turn at high way road without observing the flow of traffic on the busy road and thereby caused the accident and it is clearly borne out in the sketch, mahazar and other police records.

sentences.text: Further this respondent has issued a policy of insurance in respect of concrete mixer lorry in favour of 1st respondent and same was valid for the period from 03.08.2022 to 02.08.2023 and the liability if any is subject to the terms and conditions of policy.
Further contended that the first respondent had been willfully entrusted his vehicle to a person who did not possess valid and effective driving license to drive the same as on the date of accident.
The amount claimed by petitioners is highly exorbitant.
Hence, prays to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of above pleadings, this Tribunal framed the following:
ISSUES 1. Whether petitioners prove that they are the Legal heirs of deceased?
2. Whether petitioners prove that the son of petitioner No.1 & 2 and brother of petitioner No.3 namely Sri.Pavan Kumar.S succumbed to the injuries sustained in the accident that took place on 02.02.2023 at about 05.00 p.m., near Narayananagarada Swamy, Vivekananda Road Junction, Anjanapura Double Road, Bengaluru City,
while he was proceeding on Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-53-EU-7001 as a pillion rider, due to the rash and negligent driving of Concrete Mix Lorry bearing Regn.No.KA-05-AK-7058 by its driver?
3.
Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?
4. What order or award?
6. The petitioners in support of their case, the Petitioner No.1/father of deceased got examined himself as PW.1 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.13 and closed his side of evidence.

The medical record senior technician at Manipal Hospital got examined as PW.2 and got marked documents at Ex.P14 to Ex.P21 and one witness by name Sri.Santosh got examined as PW.3 and got marked documents at Ex.P22 and closed their side of evidence.
The respondents did not adduce their evidence either oral or documentary.

7. Heard arguments on both side and perused the materials available on records.
8.

This Tribunal answers the above issues as below:
Issue No.1 & 2: In the Affirmative. Issue No.3 : Partly in the Affirmative.
Issue No.4 :

sentences.text: Issue No.1:- It is the contention of the Petitioners that petitioner No.1 & 2 being the parents of deceased and petitioner No.3 being the brother of deceased have filed this claim petition claiming compensation for death of Mr.Pavan Kumar.S and they are the legal heirs of the deceased.
In order to prove the relationship with the deceased, the petitioners furnished Ex.P.12 & 13 i.e., Notarized copy of Marks Card and Aadhaar cards.
The documents furnished by petitioners disclose that petitioner No.1 and 2 is the father and mother of deceased and petitioner No.3 is the brother of deceased.
The documents furnished by petitioners disclose the relationship of petitioners with that of the deceased.
The respondents not furnished any materials to rebut or disprove the documents furnished by petitioners related to their relationship with the deceased.
The respondent not rebutted said documents with cogent materials.
In the cross examination of PW.1 also, nothing to disprove or rebut the contention of petitioners related to their relationship with the deceased could be elicited.
The materials placed on record disclose that the petitioners are the legal heirs of deceased Mr.Pavan Kumar.S.
Accordingly, this Tribunal answers Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.

10. Issue No.2:- It is the case of the petitioners that deceased succumbed to the injuries sustained in the accident that took place on 02.02.2023 at about 5.00 p.m., near Narayanagarada Swamy Vivekananda Road Junction, Anjanapura Double Road, Bengaluru City, while he was proceeding on Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-53-EU-7001 as a pillion rider, due to the rash and negligent driving of Concrete Mix Lorry bearing Regn.No.KA- 05-AK-7058 driven by its driver.
11. The Petitioner No.1/father of deceased Mr.Pavan Kumar.S examined as PW.1.
In the chief- examination, PW.1 deposed that his son was proceeding on a motor cycle as a pillion rider and due to the rash and negligent driving of lorry by its driver, the accident occurred.
In order to prove the accident and negligence of the driver of lorry, the petitioners produced Ex.P1
First Information lodged by rider of motor cycle by name Sri.Dommera S/o.Yallappa with police on 03.05.2023 pertaining to the accident occurred on 02.02.2023.
On the basis of first information statement lodged by rider of motor cycle, the police registered the FIR as per Ex.P.1 for the offence punishable U/s.279 & 337 of IPC.
In the first information statement as well as FIR, the accident is stated to have been caused due to rash and negligent driving of lorry by its driver.
The owner or driver of the lorry does not appear to have challenged the FIR or its contents.
In column No.6 of FIR, the driver of the lorry is shown as the accused and accident is stated to have been caused due to his negligence.
After registration of FIR, police appear to have visited the place of accident and drawn spot sketch and spot panchanama as per Ex.P.3 & 4 wherein the place of accident has been described.

In Ex.P.4,
mahazar also, it is mentioned that the accident took place due to negligence on the part of driver of lorry.
On perusal of Ex.P.3, sketch, it depicts that the lorry came to the side of the road where motorcycle appears to be travelling and collided to the motorcycle.
Ex . P.3
discloses that the accident took place towards the right side at the center of the road.
As per sketch, the lorry appears to have approached towards wrong direction.
The copy of photographs furnished along with mahazar indicates that the lorry is standing towards right from the center of the road.
The mahazar as well as sketch discloses the negligence on the part of driver of lorry in the cause of accident.
Ex.P.5 is the IMV Report, wherein the damages caused to both the vehicles are mentioned.
Ex.P.6 - Inquest Report.
Ex.P7 is the PM report, wherein deceased Mr.Pavan Kumar.S is stated to have died due to complications following multiple injuries sustained in the accident.

The I.O., after detailed investigation filed the charge sheet at Ex.P.8 against the driver of the offending vehicle for the Shankar.B vs Raghavendra Ready Mix Concrete on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145092162/

sentences.text: The final report is filed after detailed investigation in the matter and in the final report also, the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending lorry.
The owner or driver of lorry does not appear to have challenged the FIR or final report filed by the police.
In the documents furnished by petitioners, the negligence of driver of lorry appears to be the cause for the accident.
The respondents not furnished any materials contrary to the documents furnished by petitioners related to negligence of driver of offending vehicle.
The documents furnished by petitioners disclose the aspect of negligence on the part of driver of lorry in the cause of accident.

The respondents not furnished any satisfactory materials to show that the investigation is not conducted in a proper manner or to show that the factual situation is different from the one as shown in the sketch.
The materials placed by the petitioners point out towards negligence on the driver of offending lorry in the cause of accident.
The materials on record disclose the aspect of negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
The respondent No.2 contended that the accident was caused due to negligence on the part of deceased and there was no negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.
No materials are placed to substantiate the said contention.
PW.1 and PW.3 is cross examined on behalf of respondent No.2, but nothing to show negligence on the part of deceased in the cause of accident could be elicited in the cross examination of witnesses.
The respondents not furnished satisfactory materials in order to show negligence on the part of deceased in the cause of accident.
The materials placed on record do not disclose the aspect of negligence on the part of deceased in the cause of accident.
12. The respondents not placed satisfactory materials before the tribunal to disprove case of petitioner.
No satisfactory materials are placed by the respondents to disprove or rebut the documents furnished by petitioners to prove the aspect of negligence.
The materials on record are not sufficient and satisfactory to substantiate the contention of respondents related to negligence on the part of deceased in the cause of accident.
In the absence of satisfactory materials to rebut the documents, the documents furnished by the petitioners are to be considered for ascertaining the aspect of negligence.

So, the oral and documentary evidence placed by the petitioners disclose that deceased died while he was proceeding on motor cycle, due to hit by offending vehicle and points out towards negligence on the part of driver of offending lorry.

Under these circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of petitioner coupled with the documents produced before this tribunal, this tribunal is of the opinion that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Lorry bearing Regn.No.KA-05-AK-7058 by its driver and deceased succumbed to injuries.

Accordingly,
Issue No.2 is answered in the Affirmative.
13. Issue No.3:
In view of answering issue No.1 & 2 in the affirmative, the petitioners are entitled for compensation.

In order to assess the compensation, the Tribunal has to look into several factors like age, avocation, income of deceased, conveyance charges, funeral and obsequies, towards of loss of love and affection, etc.
(A) Towards dependency and loss of future earnings:
(i) In the petition the age of the deceased Mr.Pavan Kumar is shown as 23 years.
In order to prove age of deceased, the petitioners have produced Ex.P.13 - Notarized copy of Aadhaar Card, wherein his date of birth is mentioned as 04.03.1999.
The accident occurred on 02.02.2023.

As per the materials placed by the petitioners, the Shankar.B vs Raghavendra Ready Mix Concrete on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145092162/

sentences.text: age of deceased appears to be 24 years as on the date of accident.
The respondents not furnished any materials to rebut or disprove the document furnished by petitioners related to age of deceased.
In the absence of satisfactory materials, the documents furnished by petitioner are to be considered for ascertaining the age of deceased.
As such, the age of the deceased is 24 years as on the date of accident, as per the materials on record and same is taken into consideration.
As per dictum of Hon'ble Supreme court of India in Smt.Sarla Verma case the multiplier applicable in present case is '18'.
( ii )
The petitioners contended that deceased Mr.Pavan Kumar was working as Civil Engineering Contractor and earning a sum of .80,000/- per month.
In order to prove the occupation and income of deceased, the petitioners have not produced any documents.
The petitioners not furnished any satisfactory materials in order to substantiate their contention related to occupation and income of the deceased.
No materials are placed by petitioners to show the occupation and income of the deceased.
In the absence of satisfactory materials, notional income is to be taken into consideration.
By considering the facts and circumstances of case, the notional income of deceased is considered as .16,000/- per month.

In Hem Raj V/s the Oriental Insurance Company Ltd and others the Hon'ble Supreme Court held that there cannot be distinction where there is positive evidence of income and where minimum income is determined on guess work in the facts and circumstances of a case.

entities.text: Hem Raj V/s the Oriental Insurance Company Ltd and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Both the situations stand at the same footing.
In view of ratio laid down by the Hon'ble supreme court of India, the petitioners are entitled for future prospects.

National Insurance Company Ltd V/s Pranaya Sethi and others case the Hon'ble Supreme Court held that, in case the deceased was self-employed or on a fixed salary an addition of 40% of the established income should be warranted where the deceased was below 40 years.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd V/s Pranaya Sethi and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the case on hand deceased was aged about 24 years.
Hence, in view of ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court, petitioners are entitled for additional 40% to the established income.

The established income of the deceased was .16,000/- and 40% of .16,000/-
is .6,400/-.
So, the total gross income of deceased was .16,000/- + .6,400/- = .22,400/- per month.
As per the materials on record, deceased Mr.Pavan Kumar was a bachelor.

Hence as per ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in above reported judgments 50% of income of the deceased is to be deducted towards his personal expenses and 50% is to be taken as income for dependency and it comes to be .11,200/- p.m.
The petitioner No.1 & 2 are the parents and petitioner No.3 is brother of deceased.
The petitioners contended that they are dependent on the income of deceased.
On perusal of materials on record, the petitioners are considered to be the dependents of deceased.
The respondents not furnished any satisfactory materials in order to show that the petitioners are not dependent on the income of deceased.
In the cross examination of PW.1 also, nothing is elicited related to dependency of petitioners on the deceased.
As such, petitioner No.1 to 3 are considered to be dependents of deceased.

Thus, petitioners No.1 to 3 are entitled to compensation of .24,19,200/- towards loss of dependency which is calculated as follows:

( B) Towards Consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses;
In the case on hand, the date of accident was on 02.02.2023.

So, in view of ratio laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Pranay Sethi case, the petitioners are entitled for additional 10% on conventional heads which is to be enhanced on percentage basis in every three years and the enhancement should be at the rate of 10% in being the parents of deceased are entitled for .48,400/- (each) towards loss of Filial Consortium and also entitled for .18,150/- towards loss of estate .18,150/- towards funeral expenses.
(C) Towards Medical Expenses:
The petitioners claimed compensation towards medical expenses.
The petitioner No.1 contended that his son took treatment at the Hospital.
The petitioner produced Inpatient Bill for a sum of .22,18,465/- which are marked as Ex.P.10, 16 & 17.

As per the entries in Ex.P.10, 16 & 17, a sum of .6,47,215/- appears to have been sponsored by Star Health and Allied Insurance Company Limited MMH Share, .2,800/- policy discount and remaining amount for a sum of .15,68,450/- appears to have been paid by petitioner.

entities.text: Star Health and Allied Insurance Company Limited
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: In the cross examination, PW.1 admitted the aspect of disbursement of part of medical expenses by Star Health insurance company.
The petitioners are not entitled to the amount paid by Star Health insurance company and the discount amount provided by concerned hospital.
The documents furnished by petitioners disclose the aspect of treatment availed by deceased and the expenses incurred by the petitioners for the treatment.
The respondents not rebutted the medical bills by placing cogent evidence.
The respondents not furnished any satisfactory materials to controvert or rebut the documents furnished by petitioner No.1 related to the medical expenses.
In the absence of materials to the contrary, the documents furnished by petitioner No.1 is to be considered.
The materials on record do not disclose the aspect of payment of entire medical expenses by petitioners.
The part of expenses is paid by Star health insurance company which is reflected in the document itself.
The petitioners also do not appear to have disputed the aspect of payment made by said insurance company.
As such, the petitioners are not entitled to the amount paid by Star Health insurance company towards the medical expenses.
So, this tribunal is of the view that compensation of .15,68,450/- appears just and reasonable towards medical expenses.

14. Thus, the petitioners are entitled for total compensation as follows:

15. In MFA.No.100090 of 2014 C/w. MFA.No.25107 of 2013 between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs. Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another, the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka at Page No.7 at Para No.15 held as follows:
"However, the provisions of Section 149(1) of the Act to the extent they speak of interest payable on the compensation amount is in the nature of an exception to the general law enacted in 169 of the M.V.Act and therefore, the provisions of Section 34 of CPC to that extent become invocable on the general principles of construction of statutes namely the special law overrides the general law.

entities.text: Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs. Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, in the absence of any other law relating to interest on Judgments, the MACT has to follow the provisions of Section 34 of CPC, 1908.

Thus, in the given circumstances of this case,
interest at the rate of more than 6% could not have been awarded."

In view of ratio and dictum laid down by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in the above judgment, the petitioners are entitled for interest @ 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
16. The petitioner has filed petition against the respondent No.1 & 2.
It is already held that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Lorry bearing Regn.No.KA-05-AK-7058 by its driver.
So, the respondent No.1 and 2 being the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, Issue No.3 answered Partly in the Affirmative.
17. Issue No.4:

In view of the findings given on the above said issues, this tribunal proceed to pass the following:
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioners Under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioners are entitled for total compensation amount of .41,20,750/-
(Rupees Forty One Lakhs Twenty Thousand Seven Hundred and Fifty only) with interest at 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realization.

sentences.text: Respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
Respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to deposit the said compensation amount within a period of two months from the date of award.

Out of the total compensation amount, the petitioner No.1 & 2 being the Parents of deceased are entitled for 40% each and petitioner No.3 being the brother of deceased is entitled for 20% of the compensation amount.

In total amount apportioned to the share of petitioner No.1 to 3, 60% of the amount shall be released in favour of petitioner No.1 to 3, and 40% of the amount shall be kept in FD for a period of three years.

After deposit of compensation amount with interest thereon disburse amount as mentioned above as per guidelines laid down by Hon'ble High Court in MFA No.2509/2019 (ECA) and as per General Circular No.2/2019 dated 19.8.2019.

Bank shall not advance loan on such FD, and shall not cause premature release of FD without permission from the Tribunal.

Bank shall release amount along with interest thereon in favour of petitioners on proper verification and identification or credit said amount to their account after expiry of three years period of deposit, without waiting for further order of court.
The advocate fee is fixed at .1,000/-.

5. On the basis of above pleadings, this Tribunal framed the following:

In the absence of satisfactory materials to rebut the documents, the documents furnished by the petitioners are to be considered for ascertaining the aspect of negligence.
In the absence of satisfactory materials, the documents furnished by petitioner are to be considered for ascertaining the age of deceased.

In order to prove the occupation and income of deceased, the petitioners have not produced any documents.
The petitioners not furnished any satisfactory materials in order to substantiate their contention related to occupation and income of the deceased.

National Insurance Company Ltd V/s Pranaya Sethi and others case the Hon'ble Supreme Court held that, in case the deceased was self-employed or on a fixed salary an addition of 40% of the established income should be warranted where the deceased was below 40 years.
So, this tribunal is of the view that compensation of .15,68,450/- appears just and reasonable towards medical expenses.
